What Table 2's 31.76\% figure adds is a specific, falsifiable answer to a question -- how much of this specific literature, assembled by this specific search, reports data at all -- that a different reviewer running the same search could check and, if the underlying corpus has changed, update.

Corpus characteristics (Table 2) describe what that corpus looks like: recent, well-indexed, and -- the finding the rest of the paper is built around -- only 31.76\% of it shows any marker of reported data in its own abstract
This review does not re-classify either cited study individually; they are included as concrete illustrations of the corpus's texture, not as evidence for or against the 31.76\% figure itself.

Combined with the 68.63\% share published in 2023 or later, the corpus this review characterises is not one field with an established venue structure but a rapidly assembling one: most venues in it contributed a small handful of records, and most of those records are recent enough that citation counts (median 62) have not had long to accumulate

The 31.76\% empirical-marker share is consequently a property of a topic as it appears scattered across a heterogeneous mix of venue types, not a property of a defined sub-field with its own reporting norms -- a distinction worth naming because a reader might otherwise expect a specialist venue's editorial norms to push authors toward reporting data, and the corpus's dispersion is itself evidence

Appendix B documents in detail why individual studies' reported returns are not comparable to each other; the same problem bears directly on how a reader should treat the 31.76\% figure, and it is worth stating in the main body rather than leaving it only as background

The 31.76\% figure is consequently an upper bound not just on how much of the corpus reports data in general, as Section 3.2 establishes, but specifically an upper bound on how much of the corpus could even in principle support a denominator-comparable ROI figure, since every denominator-comparable figure is empirical in Section 2's sense but not every abstract clearing Section 2's bar reports a d

Table 1's funnel moves from 2,000 identified records to 1,893 unique to 1,779 screened -- a loss of about 11\% before any empirical-content judgement is made, entirely from deduplication and missing abstracts

It is reported for the same reason every other stage of the funnel is reported: so a reader auditing the 31.76\% figure can see exactly how many records fed into it and at what stage each one was excluded, rather than being handed a single ratio with no visible construction.

The two exclusion mechanisms -- deduplication and missing-abstract screening -- together account for all 221 records excluded between identification and the screened corpus, and they are worth distinguishing because they carry different implications for the 31.76\% figure's reliability

Missing-abstract exclusion is different in kind: a record with no reconstructable abstract cannot be screened for a data-reporting marker at all, so its true empirical status, whatever it is, is simply absent from the 31.76\% calculation rather than counted against it

What the current measurement does establish is a lower bound on how much this reviewer's search strategy specifically found: at least 68.24\% of a corpus built this way shows no abstract-level marker of reported data, and no pooled ROI synthesis should be attempted over a literature with that property until the marker-level screening here is replaced by a full-text audit -- itself the natural next

If a broader search strategy found a higher empirical share than 31.76\%, the field would still not automatically support pooling -- the denominator problem in Section 3.3 is orthogonal to how many studies report data at all, and a higher share of data-reporting abstracts does not by itself resolve whether those studies report comparable returns

The asymmetry matters: this review's central recommendation, that practitioners should not expect a literature-wide ROI benchmark from the current published record, is robust to the direction most plausible revisions would move the number, even though the exact figure of 31.76\% is specific to the search strategy documented in Section 2.
